title: Quasi-projectivity descends along an arbitrary field extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: If X_K is quasi-projective over K for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is quasi-projective over k (statement lines 2816-2821). The proof unpacks the definition into the three obligations and discharges them one at a time: for an affine open Spec(A) of X the base change is an affine open of X_K whose coordinate ring is a finitely generated K-algebra, so A is a finitely generated k-algebra by descent of finite generation; quasi-compactness descends by taking the image of the quasi-compact X_K; and the existence of a g-ample invertible sheaf for a finite type morphism is equivalent to having an ample invertible sheaf, which then descends along the field extension by the ample descent lemma (proof lines 2824-2841). The claim is H2: three bookkeeping steps, each resting on one cited result, with the equivalence between relative ampleness for a finite type morphism and the existence of an ample invertible sheaf as the organizing observation.
